name: Voltas Ltd
title: Voltas Ltd - 500575 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Voltas Q4 FY26 consolidated PBT fell to INR 181 crores from INR 343 crores as UCP margins were hit by commodity inflation and rupee depreciation.
summary.overview: Consolidated total income rose marginally to INR 4,930 crores in Q4 FY26 from INR 4,847 crores, but PBT fell to INR 181 crores and net profit to INR 113 crores from INR 343 crores and INR 236 crores. For FY26, total income fell to INR 14,483 crores from INR 15,737 crores, PBT to INR 557 crores from INR 1,191 crores, and net profit to INR 377 crores from INR 834 crores. Management said March 2026 was a record sales month and April was close to that level, but margins were compressed by old-cost inventory, FX losses and commodity inflation, with price hikes only partly passed through so far.

segments.name: Segment A - UCP (RAC, CAC, CR, AR, Voltbek)
segments.commentary: FY26 RAC volume was 2.25 million units; Voltas leads the No. 2 player by a 5.1% primary market share gap. Margins were hit in Q1-Q2 by channel overhang and in Q4 by commodity inflation and rupee depreciation. Chennai plant utilisation is ~1.2 lakh units/month against 1.5 million units annual capacity.

segments.name: Voltbek (within Segment A)
segments.commentary: Year-to-date market share of 8.6% in washing machines and 6.2% in refrigerators in a sluggish market. Sanand plant localisation is ongoing and management expects margin expansion over the medium term.

segments.name: Segment B - Electro-Mechanical Projects (MEP)
segments.commentary: Order book close to INR 6,200 crores at 31 March 2026, of which ~INR 4,500 crores is domestic. Management says 40-50% of the India MEP book and some international contracts carry price variation clauses, so commodity and labour inflation is passed through. No client has invoked force majeure; Qatar force majeure was revoked.

segments.name: Segment C - Mining, Construction & Textile Machinery
segments.commentary: Mining and construction equipment showed steady top-line growth, supported by crushing and screening demand and Mozambique operations. Textile machinery was weak amid cautious capex sentiment, with management pinning hopes on Union Budget 2026 and PLI support for spinning recovery.

guidance_outlook: UCP margins: management said the target is a gradual step-up towards FY25 levels (UCP margin ~8.4% in FY25 vs ~3.2% in FY26, per analyst); no firm FY27 margin number given, and no timeline for returning to FY25 levels.
Q4 FY26 margins: management said it is not expecting any sharp downturn in margin profile for the quarter (Q1 FY27), with costs hitting progressively as a mix of pre-war and post-war costs.

Pricing: further price increases are planned, depending on rupee-dollar, war and commodity moves; management said it is watching prices almost weekly and sees double-digit inflation, to be passed through as costs hit. Pass-through expected for most brands.

Demand: industry RAC expected to grow at least 15-20% in FY27 off a weak FY26 base (industry FY26 degrowth ~10-12%, 14.3 million primary units); commercial refrigeration expected to grow upwards of 10%; commercial AC expected to grow 12-15%.
Medium-term: Voltbek expected to steadily improve brand preference, penetration and operating leverage over the medium term; management expects margin expansion at Sanand over time.

Capacity and capex: small capex to lift Chennai from 1.5 million to 2 million units is ready; third investment round deferred 1-2 years until demand is visible. Capex focus remains on Segment A (capacity, R&D, CAC).
capex_capacity: Chennai plant built to 1.5 million units capacity (up from 1 million last year), running at about 1.2 lakh units per month; a small capex to take it to 2 million units is ready, with the third investment round deferred 1-2 years until demand is visible.
Pantnagar and Chennai facilities running at higher utilisation than last year.
Ongoing capex in factory automation, warehouse rationalisation and integrated inventory planning.
Capex is mostly directed at Segment A (capacity and R&D); CAC is a key area for capex deployment.
Sanand plant localisation and scale-up for Voltbek is in progress.
demand_pricing: Price hikes: new BEE table products (from March) carried 5% on 3-star (~75% mix) and 10% on 5-star (~25% mix), a blended ~6-7%, plus a further 1-2% (copper) and another increase in the latest month, linked to rupee depreciation.
GST on RAC cut from 28% to 18% cushions consumer affordability this summer versus last year.
Channel inventory is under 45 days and closer to 30 days, per management.
March 2026 was a record sales month in company history; April was close to that level and May is tracking well. Secondary sales are picking up as the higher-priced stock is absorbed.
Competition: about 60 brands in RAC; management said the company holds a 5.1% primary share lead over the next cluster of four brands.

qa_highlights.question: How should margins for UCP be modelled for FY27 and FY28, given UCP margin of ~3.2% in FY26 against 8.4% in FY25?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q1-Q2 margins were hit by a channel stock overhang from erratic summer and early monsoon, and that some pressures are structural (supply chain, currency). The aim is gradual improvement towards FY25 levels, through pricing and cost actions.

qa_highlights.question: Why did gross margin fall only ~85 bps while segment margins fell sharply?
qa_highlights.answer: No direct reconciliation was given. Management pointed to the Q1-Q2 overhang and later commodity and FX pressures as the drivers of the segment drop.

qa_highlights.question: What was the impact of the ~INR 55 crore FX loss in H2, how much hit Q4, and how much extra marketing was spent?
qa_highlights.answer: Q4 still used the mix of old and new inventory: old stock was consumed in the first 4-6 weeks of the quarter. Marketing was managed within the existing pool and was broadly comparable, with brand ambassador costs the only extra item. The FX share in Q4 was not quantified.

qa_highlights.question: Will cost inflation hit Q1 margins and could they dip significantly before price increases?
qa_highlights.answer: Costs will hit progressively, a mix of pre-war and post-war costs. Management expects no sharp margin downturn in the quarter, with more price actions to follow. Unallocated costs rose on forex and treasury mark-to-market.

qa_highlights.question: Can you quantify price actions and provide RAC volume and the MEP domestic/international order book split?
qa_highlights.answer: Price actions are detailed above. FY26 RAC volume was 2.25 million units. The order book is ~INR 6,200 crores, of which ~INR 4,500 crores is domestic.

qa_highlights.question: Has the company seen force majeure or margin risk in the MEP business from metal price moves?
qa_highlights.answer: No client has invoked force majeure; Qatar's temporary contractor option was revoked. Price variation clauses cover 40-50% of the India MEP book and some international contracts, so margin risk is limited.

qa_highlights.question: What is channel inventory and Chennai utilisation, and what is the domestic share of the order book?
qa_highlights.answer: Channel inventory is under 45 days, closer to 30. Chennai runs at ~1.2 lakh units per month against 1.5 million units annual capacity. The domestic order book is ~INR 4,500 crores.

risks_watch: Commodity (copper, aluminium, plastics, gas) and rupee-dollar moves could drive further double-digit price increases and a demand hit if affordability weakens.
Margin recovery depends on pricing pass-through and on the old-cost inventory running out; Q1 FY27 margins are the first test.
Unallocated costs, including forex and treasury mark-to-market, rose sharply in Q4 and need to be tracked.
Middle East conflict affects the international MEP business through travel, logistics, collections and execution; Qatar force majeure was revoked.
Textile machinery remains weak; recovery depends on policy support and PLI expansion.
Inventory was moderately elevated at Q4 end and is expected to normalise as seasonal demand builds.
summary.management_tone: Confident on demand and the season, with management calling March a record and April and May strong. More cautious on margins: they describe recovery as gradual, with pressures called structural and no firm FY27 margin number given.
key_quotes: So, the trend is certainly on an upward trajectory, but the only saving grace was that, that reduction in GST, which was tantamount to a 7.8% on selling price, 10% reduction is equal to 7.8% on MOP.
We are seriously talking about double-digit inflation. And it will get passed through as and when the costs start hitting us.
We are not expecting any sharp downturn in terms of the margin profile for the quarter.
March was a superb month. It was a record high in our entire history.

adds.what: Chennai plant to 2 million units from 1.5 million (small capex, ready)

growth.why: Management guides RAC industry growth of at least 15-20% in FY27 off a weak FY26 base, backed by a ready small capex to lift Chennai to 2 million units, ~INR 6,200 crore MEP order book, and price pass-through; margin recovery toward FY25 levels is gradual with no firm number or timeline.
